params.body:
The app's voice screen can type to the workbench as well. Spoken and typed lines are one conversation, the same one Portal shows on the desk and the phone.

- The screen draws the bridge's timeline (`GET /thread`). It reads every four seconds while the screen is shown, and every 1.5 seconds while an answer is coming. Lines said a moment ago and the workbench's notices stay until the bridge has them.
- Each line says how it came: spoken, typed (by you) or written (by the voice). Spoken lines are a shade quieter, as they are transcripts.
- A composer sits above the call controls, with or without the voice on. While this phone holds the live voice, a typed line goes into that session and the voice answers it out loud (`held`). A line typed on another device reaches it through `/changes?conversation=`. Without a voice, the bridge answers in writing.
- Online only: without a network, or with the workbench out of reach, the box is off and says why. A line that was not taken stays in the box.
- New: `voice/Conversation.kt`. `Bridge` gets `thread()` and `say()`, and `changes()` now takes the conversation. Strings are English only.

Checked: `assembleDebug` and `testDebugUnitTest` pass. The voice mockup (`build/mockups/7-voice.png`) now shows spoken and typed lines with the composer.

Needs the portal-cli pull request on the same branch name.
params.title: Type to the workbench on the voice screen, one conversation with the voice
